title: Tenant Urgency Index for Model Deprecation: telemetry, thresholds, and migration playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: define and deliver a per-tenant 'Urgency Index' that quantifies how urgently each customer should be migrated off a model that is being deprecated or degraded. The index will drive automated notifications, prioritized migration tickets, and prescriptive runbooks (auto-fallback, dedicated capacity offers, CSM outreach). Scope: hosted + dedicated customers; initial rollout for enterprise tenants (> $10k/month) with phased rollout to mid-market. Excludes on-prem private deployments for now (different upgrade cadence).
background: We have ad-hoc deprecation and fallback playbooks today. Sales/CS and Solutions teams repeatedly ask: who should we prioritize when a model variant is sunset or an external model has an availability shock? Current triage is manual and reactive; this ticket designs an objective telemetry-driven index so engineering, support, and GTM have a shared, measurable prioritization signal.
decision_rationale: Use a signals-weighted score (0-100) rather than simple rule sets so we can rank large customer populations and tune weights per cohort. Prioritize signals that reflect both reliability (SLO breaches, error rate, fallback frequency) and business exposure (monthly spend, SLA tier, production traffic ratio). Keep initial formula interpretable and decouple from billing systems for speed of implementation.
telemetry_signals: SLO latency breach rate (p95 > target) — 25pt weight
Token error rate (5xx/timeout) normalized over 7d — 20pt weight
Fallback frequency to alternative model (last 14d) — 15pt weight
Quality regressions (eval prompt set failure rate increase) — 15pt weight
Active production traffic ratio (share of customer requests hitting deprecated model) — 10pt weight
Recent rollback frequency (deploy toggles for same model) — 5pt weight
scoring_formula: Score = sum(weighted signal buckets). Each signal maps to 0-100 bucket then multiplied by its weight fraction. Example: if latency breach maps to 80 and its max weight is 25 => contributes 20. Final score normalized to 0-100. Implement server-side computed score in Observability service and expose in Tenant profile API.
tiers: Critical (80-100): immediate migration playbook + account outreach within 24h
High (60-79): automated fallback + CSM notification within 48h
Medium (35-59): prepare migration ticket and runbook; monitor for 7 days
Low (0-34): informational alert; surface in weekly capacity planning
runbook_steps: Critical: 1) Auto-enable compatible fallback model variant; 2) Open high-priority migration ticket (ENG-queue); 3) CSM + Solutions notify customer with migration timeline and optional dedicated capacity offer; 4) Schedule accelerated rollout and QA
High: 1) Toggle non-intrusive fallback and increase caching to reduce impact; 2) Notify CSM and SRE; 3) Create migration backlog item with expected 2-week window
Medium: 1) Generate migration guidance doc auto-populated with tenant telemetry; 2) Add to low-priority migration sprint; 3) Re-evaluate score weekly
Low: 1) Surface in console 'Model Health' with suggested non-urgent actions
metrics_to_track: Index coverage (percentage of tenants with computed score)
True positive rate: fraction of Critical/High scores that later triggered actual customer-impacting incidents
Number of automated fallbacks executed successfully
stakeholders: Eng: Luca Moreno (assignee), Priya Shah (Observability), Daniel Kim (Runtime)
risks_and_tradeoffs: False positives: too many Critical classifications could overwhelm SRE/CSM — mitigate by conservative initial weights and manual gating for top-5 customers
Privacy/contract constraints: enterprise tenants may require opt-out or different notification cadence — handle via tenant metadata and policy checks
Operational cost: running per-tenant scoring at scale adds compute; implement sampling and incremental scoring for low-traffic tenants
acceptance_criteria: Index computed for 95% of enterprise tenants for the last 30 days
Dashboard shows real-time scores and history; stakeholders can filter by region and tier
Automated Critical path for a synthetic test tenant completes end-to-end (fallback, ticket creation, notifications)
GTM materials (CSM playbook + customer email templates) are reviewed and approved
